```{ojs}
//| output: false
// How often a posted price moved, not by how much. `changed` compares a
// station's previous OBSERVED reading, so the denominator is transitions we
// actually saw -- never calendar days, which we did not always look at.
changesWindowDays = 90
```

```{ojs}
// Its own chunk, and NOT `output: false`: the control shared that flag with the
// constant above it, so the drill-down existed in the DOM at zero by zero
// pixels and no one could reach the per-station view behind it.
viewof changesPlace = asField(
  Inputs.select(["All US states", ...changesStates], {
    label: "Drill into",
    value: "All US states"
  }),
  {inline: true}
)
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
changesStates = {
  const seen = new Set();
  for (const station of stationsAll) {
    if (station.country === "US" && station.region) seen.add(station.region);
  }
  return [...seen].sort();
}

// State grain: one cell per (chain, state, day).
changesByState = db
  ? await db.query(`
      WITH win AS (
        SELECT station_key, brand, capture_date, changed
        FROM history
        WHERE grade = ${sqlText(grade)}
          AND capture_date > (SELECT max(capture_date) FROM history) - ${changesWindowDays}
      ),
      scoped AS (
        SELECT w.brand, s.region, w.station_key, w.capture_date, w.changed
        FROM win w JOIN stations s ON s.station_key = w.station_key
        WHERE s.country = 'US' AND s.region IS NOT NULL
      )
      SELECT brand,
             region,
             strftime(capture_date, '%Y-%m-%d') AS d,
             count(*) FILTER (WHERE changed IS NOT NULL) AS n_obs,
             count(*) FILTER (WHERE changed)             AS n_changed,
             count(DISTINCT station_key)                 AS n_stations
      FROM scoped
      GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
      ORDER BY brand, region, d
    `)
  : []

// Station grain, for one state. station_key leads the parquet's sort order, so
// this prunes row groups rather than scanning.
changesStationKeys = {
  if (changesPlace === "All US states") return [];
  return stationsAll
    .filter((s) => s.country === "US" && s.region === changesPlace)
    .map((s) => s.station_key);
}

changesByStation = db && changesStationKeys.length
  ? await db.query(`
      SELECT station_key,
             brand,
             strftime(capture_date, '%Y-%m-%d') AS d,
             count(*) FILTER (WHERE changed IS NOT NULL) AS n_obs,
             count(*) FILTER (WHERE changed)             AS n_changed
      FROM history
      WHERE station_key IN (${sqlList(changesStationKeys)})
        AND grade = ${sqlText(grade)}
        AND capture_date > (SELECT max(capture_date) FROM history) - ${changesWindowDays}
      GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
      ORDER BY station_key, d
    `)
  : []
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Every day between the first and the last, whether or not it has a row. A band
// scale takes its domain from the data, so a collection gap would close up and
// the axis would say time was continuous when it was not.
function changesDomain(rows) {
  const days = rows.map((r) => r.d).filter((d) => d);
  if (!days.length) return [];
  const first = new Date(days.reduce((a, b) => (a < b ? a : b)) + "T00:00:00Z");
  const last = new Date(days.reduce((a, b) => (a > b ? a : b)) + "T00:00:00Z");
  const out = [];
  for (let t = new Date(first); t <= last; t.setUTCDate(t.getUTCDate() + 1)) {
    out.push(t.toISOString().slice(0, 10));
  }
  return out;
}

// Past roughly one cell per 3px the days stop fitting, so they bin into ISO
// weeks. Binning sums the counts rather than averaging the rates: a mean of
// rates would weight a thin day the same as a full one.
changesMaxBins = Math.max(14, Math.floor((chartWidth - 46) / 3))

function isoWeek(day) {
  const d = new Date(day + "T00:00:00Z");
  const thursday = new Date(d);
  thursday.setUTCDate(d.getUTCDate() + 3 - ((d.getUTCDay() + 6) % 7));
  const first = new Date(Date.UTC(thursday.getUTCFullYear(), 0, 4));
  const week =
    1 + Math.round(((thursday - first) / 86400000 - 3 + ((first.getUTCDay() + 6) % 7)) / 7);
  return `${thursday.getUTCFullYear()}-W${String(week).padStart(2, "0")}`;
}

function changesBinned(rows, keyName) {
  const domain = changesDomain(rows);
  const weekly = domain.length > changesMaxBins;
  const bins = new Map();
  for (const row of rows) {
    const bin = weekly ? isoWeek(row.d) : row.d;
    const key = [row[keyName], row.brand, bin].join(" :: ");
    const cell = bins.get(key) || {
      key: row[keyName],
      brand: row.brand,
      bin,
      n_obs: 0,
      n_changed: 0,
      n_stations: 0
    };
    cell.n_obs += Number(row.n_obs) || 0;
    cell.n_changed += Number(row.n_changed) || 0;
    cell.n_stations = Math.max(cell.n_stations, Number(row.n_stations) || 0);
    bins.set(key, cell);
  }
  const cells = [...bins.values()].map((cell) => ({
    ...cell,
    // Absent is not unchanged. A thin cell gets no colour rather than a
    // confident 0%, because one observation is not a rate.
    rate: cell.n_obs >= 3 ? cell.n_changed / cell.n_obs : null
  }));
  const binDomain = weekly ? [...new Set(domain.map(isoWeek))] : domain;
  return {cells, binDomain, weekly};
}
```


## How often the price moved
::: {.cgp-panel}

```{ojs}
// `labelOf` names a row. A station row is keyed on its station_key and shows
// its name: keyed on the name, two stations sharing one would merge.
function changesChart(rows, keyName, {rowLabel, marginLeft, labelOf = (key) => key}) {
  const {cells, binDomain} = changesBinned(rows, keyName);
  if (!cells.length) return null;
  const brands = [...new Set(cells.map((c) => c.brand))].sort();
  // Keep at least 140px of plot area, the way compare's dotPlot does.
  const left = Math.min(marginLeft, Math.max(56, chartWidth - 24 - 140));

  return brands.map((brand) => {
    const mine = cells.filter((c) => c.brand === brand);
    // Each chain's rows are its own. Shared, every chart carried a blank row
    // for each of the other chain's stations. Sorted by what the row shows, as
    // before, with the key breaking a tie between two stations of one name.
    const keys = [...new Set(mine.map((c) => c.key))].sort((a, b) => {
      const [x, y] = [labelOf(a), labelOf(b)];
      return x < y ? -1 : x > y ? 1 : a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0;
    });
    return Plot.plot({
      width: chartWidth,
      // The day labels are turned 35 degrees, and a turned "2026-09-17" hangs
      // about 50px below the axis: in Plot's default 30px gutter the bottom of
      // every one was cut off.
      height: 58 + keys.length * (chartWidth < 520 ? 11 : 16),
      marginLeft: left,
      marginRight: 24,
      marginTop: 28,
      marginBottom: 54,
      style: {background: "transparent", color: palette.text},
      x: {
        domain: binDomain,
        label: null,
        ticks: Math.min(8, binDomain.length),
        tickRotate: -35
      },
      y: {domain: keys, label: null, tickFormat: labelOf},
      ariaLabel: `${
        BRAND_NAMES[brand] || brand
      }: how often the posted ${GRADE_LABELS[grade]} price moved, by ${rowLabel}`,
      marks: [
        Plot.cell(mine, {
          x: "bin",
          y: "key",
          // A function fill gets an identity colour scale, so these follow
          // Quarto's light/dark toggle the way the map's markers do.
          fill: (c) => (c.rate == null ? palette.missing : colorForFraction(c.rate, palette)),
          title: (c) =>
            `${labelOf(c.key)} · ${c.bin}\n` +
            (c.rate == null
              ? `not enough readings (${c.n_obs})`
              : `${fmtShare(c.rate * 100)} of ${c.n_obs} readings moved`),
          inset: 0.5
        }),
        Plot.text([BRAND_NAMES[brand] || brand], {
          frameAnchor: "top-left",
          dy: -14,
          fontWeight: 600,
          fill: palette.text
        })
      ]
    });
  });
}

changesFigure = {
  if (!db) {
    return html`<div class="cgp-notice cgp-station-chart">Loading the price database…</div>`;
  }
  const drilled = changesPlace !== "All US states";
  const rows = drilled ? changesByStation : changesByState;
  if (!rows.length) {
    return html`<div class="cgp-notice">No ${GRADE_LABELS[grade]} history yet${
      drilled ? ` for ${changesPlace}` : ""
    }. This fills in as captures accumulate.</div>`;
  }
  const nameOf = new Map(stationsAll.map((s) => [s.station_key, s.name]));
  const charts = changesChart(rows, drilled ? "station_key" : "region", {
    rowLabel: drilled ? "station" : "state",
    marginLeft: drilled ? 150 : 56,
    labelOf: drilled ? (key) => nameOf.get(key) || key : undefined
  });
  if (!charts) return html`<div class="cgp-notice">Not enough readings yet.</div>`;
  return html`<div>${changesKeyEl()}${changesSummary}${charts}</div>`;
}

// What a cell's color means. The fill is a function, so Plot draws no legend
// of its own, and a cell's numbers are in a tooltip that a touch screen or a
// keyboard never raises: the blue, amber, red and gray were explained nowhere
// on the page. The swatches are the very colors the cells are drawn in, in
// either theme.
function changesKeyEl() {
  return html`<div class="cgp-legend cgp-changes-key">
    <span class="cgp-legend-end">0%</span>${palette.ramp.map(
      (color) => html`<span class="cgp-swatch" style=${"background:" + color}></span>`
    )}<span class="cgp-legend-end">100%</span>
    <span class="cgp-legend-note">share of the readings in a cell where the posted price had
      moved since the station's previous reading</span>
    <span class="cgp-legend-missing"><span class="cgp-swatch" style=${
      "background:" + palette.missing
    }></span> fewer than 3 readings</span>
  </div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// One line where a paragraph would go. Both counts print, because the chain
// with the flakier feed scores higher and a reader should be able to see it.
changesSummary = {
  const rows = changesPlace === "All US states" ? changesByState : changesByStation;
  const totals = new Map();
  for (const row of rows) {
    const t = totals.get(row.brand) || {obs: 0, changed: 0};
    t.obs += Number(row.n_obs) || 0;
    t.changed += Number(row.n_changed) || 0;
    totals.set(row.brand, t);
  }
  const parts = [...totals.entries()]
    .sort()
    .filter(([, t]) => t.obs > 0)
    .map(
      ([brand, t]) =>
        `${BRAND_NAMES[brand] || brand} ${fmtShare((t.changed / t.obs) * 100)} of ` +
        `${t.obs.toLocaleString()} readings`
    );
  return parts.length ? html`<div class="cgp-notice">${parts.join(" · ")}</div>` : "";
}
```
